summary: Intermittent streaming cutoffs and 504s for single-shot requests with very deep context + large output budget
description: Issue summary: Customer reports their single-shot generation requests (very large context + large max_tokens) are intermittently returning HTTP 504 or abruptly terminating the streaming connection after ~60-90s. Impact: VeraHealth has a nightly batch which processes long clinical transcripts and expects completions; jobs fail ~30% of the time causing downstream delays and billing anomalies. Environment: prod us-east using hosted API, API key scoped to customer account, observed on both redwood-13b-q4-8bit and open-llama-15b-quant. Observed since 2026-03-10 after a configuration change in the serving pool allocation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer API key and call /v1/generate with model redwood-13b-q4-8bit
2) Provide a single context concatenating ~180k tokens (multiple transcripts) in the input_text field
3) Set max_tokens to 40k and stream=true and await response
4) Repeat the request 10 times; observe 2-4 requests fail with HTTP 504 or stream close at ~60-90s
expected_behavior: Requests with large context and large output budgets should either complete or hit documented per-request token limits with clear 4xx response; streaming connections should remain open until completion or graceful error.
actual_behavior: Intermittent HTTP 504 from gateway and abrupt stream termination without structured error payload; customer sees partial token output and then connection close. Billing shows full request charged in some aborted cases.
logs_and_snippets: gateway trace ID: gt-0a9f2c3b (2026-03-13T02:14:57Z) -> upstream served until 00:01:05 then 504
serving-runtime logs (approx): [2026-03-13T02:13:12Z] request-start id=rt-8912 tokens_in=179842; [2026-03-13T02:14:17Z] finalizer-queue wait=24s; [2026-03-13T02:14:57Z] connection-reset-by-peer
No consistent OOM or GPU eviction in the node logs; scheduler shows transient backlog spikes on the pool servicing this customer's traffic.
comments: Maya Thompson (Support) 2026-03-12: Opened with customer logs and batch examples. Customer says failure rate increased after 2026-03-10. Requested sample payloads and timestamps.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-13: Initial triage — observed increased queueing and finalizer latency on pool-p-08. Hypothesis: burst of long-running generations caused finalizer/backpressure interactions with the streaming proxy leading to idle timeouts.
Customer (VeraHealth) 2026-03-13: Provided three failed request traces and confirmed identical behaviour across two models. Needs workaround to keep nightly jobs running.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-14: Reproduced locally with synthetic 160k token context and 30k max_tokens; when concurrent backlog >8, stream closed after 70-95s. Raising priority and involving runtime team.
investigation_notes: 1) Reproduction: Confirmed intermittent stream cutoffs with high-context, large-output single-shot requests when pool backlog and finalizer queueing exceed SLO thresholds.
2) Metrics: finalizer_queue_time and stream_idle_time spiked correlated with gateway 504s. No GPU OOMs; CPU and network within expected ranges except elevated proxy connection resets.

3) Hypothesis: The finalizer (post-tokenization flush and KV serialization) can be delayed by concurrent long generations; streaming proxy has comparatively low idle timeout leading to race where the client sees a connection close before the runtime completes last flush.
4) Billing anomaly: some aborted requests are being billed at full cost due to downstream accounting marking request as accepted early.
resolution_notes: - Short-term: reduce max_tokens to <=16k or split the generation into multiple smaller streamed segments. This reduced failures to <2% in customer tests.
- Medium-term: request to use a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) to avoid cross-tenant backlog spikes; offered trial for two nights.
- Runtime: adding an explicit keepalive/ping between finalizer and streaming proxy to prevent idle timeout races (PR linked).
- Gateway: increasing stream idle timeout for affected pools by config to 120s as stop-gap.
- Billing: engineering will patch accounting to only bill completed token counts for aborted streams in next billing cycle to correct customer charges.
- Postmortem to include telemetry knobs for finalizer queue depth and stream idle latency (assigned to Diego).
- Engineering change and rollout planned 2026-03-20 with canary in us-east before global rollout.
